details:
This package is a trojanized clone of @whiskeysockets/baileys published under the scope @skycodee: the legitimate Baileys source tree is republished with added code that silently forces the installing user's own WhatsApp account to subscribe to third-party channels. On connection the socket fetches remote configuration and queries newsletter IDs without the user's knowledge:
- lib/Utils/messages-media.js exports loadBase(), which builds a URL from a base64 literal ("[encoded-url-redacted]") resolving to hxxps://raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/skyzopedia/Screaper/refs/heads/main/idChannel[.]json, fetches the list, then calls the follow operation on each newsletter ID with a 5s pause between calls, inside an 80-second timer.
- lib/Socket/socket.js defines socketConnect(), which rebuilds a URL via String.fromCharCode over a decimal char-code array resolving to hxxps://raw[.]github[.]com/skyzopedia/NewsletterID/refs/heads/main/VIP_Push[.]json, fetches that list and sends a "w:mex" IQ query (query_id 7871414976211147, variables.newsletter_id) for each entry inside a 200-second timer. It is invoked right after the WhatsApp handshake in the connect path.
- lib/Socket/newsletter.js invokes loadBase() on the newsletter subsystem and exposes the follow/unfollow wrappers the payload drives. The fork also injects an operator-owned channel into user traffic: in lib/Utils/messages.js, prepareMediaMessage builds a default Message.annotations block containing newsletterJid "120363409159786018@newsletter" with newsletterName "skyzopedia", so outgoing media messages carry a reference to that channel when the caller supplied no annotations. The tampering is visible in editor-backup leftovers that were shipped in the tarball: lib/Socket/Client/websocket.js.bak still contains "this.socket.newsletterFollow(\"120363302042233203@newsletter\")" inside connect(), which was replaced in the live lib/Socket/Client/websocket.js; lib/Types/Newsletter.js.bak is the matching backup of an edited type file. The package also declares a runtime dependency on @skycodee/libsignal (a fork of libsignal published under the same scope), so installing it pulls that separately flagged package into the dependency tree.
